newsitem.title: FRANCE: French group sues Megret over race comment.
newsitem.headline: French group sues Megret over race comment.

text.p: France's Movement against Racism (MRAP) said on Tuesday it was taking legal action against the far-right National Front Party's number two, Bruno Megret, for espousing racial inequality.
"Inequality between races is patent," Megret said in a television interview on Monday, echoing National Front leader Jean-Marie Le Pen who said last year that racial inequality was "a fact".
"Once again the National Front has expressed its racist ideology," MRAP said. "In the face of this fresh provocation... MRAP has decided to lodge a complaint through its lawyer."
The legal action appeared to be doomed as a legal loophole had prevented the government from prosecuting Le Pen for his similar comment.
MRAP urged the government to revive plans to stiffen laws which punish statements directed against a particular race group but do not cover general verbal attacks.
The government has shelved a bill to widen the grounds for prosecution of racist statements and stiffening punishment, which were drafted as a response to Le Pen's comments.
The bill had been criticised as double-edged and opening the way to restriction of freedom of expression.
Megret made headlines last week when his wife Catherine was elected mayor of Vitrolles, the fourth French town to come under National Front control.
Megret himself was barred from running after exceeding the legal limits on campaign spending in an earlier campaign, but his wife made no bones about saying he would effectively run the town.
